chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a boy or a girl is born to you, sacrifice for him on the seventh day a sheep or a camel, eat from it, feed [others], name [him], shave his head on the seventh day, and give in charity the weight of his hair in gold or silver, and give to the midwife a portion of that. So whatever of that you do, it has sufficed you.

key_terms.جَزُوراً: A camel (specifically a young female camel)
key_terms.عُقَّ: Aqeeqa, the ritual sacrifice for a newborn

ai.seo_question: What are the steps and timing for performing Aqeeqa for a newborn in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of Aqeeqa on the seventh day, linking it closely with the rituals of naming and head-shaving to mark the child's entry into the community. It emphasizes social welfare by mandating charity equal to the weight of the hair in gold or silver and ensuring the midwife receives a share, reflecting the Shia emphasis on gratitude and communal support. The phrase 'أَيَّ ذَلِكَ فَعَلْتَ فَقَدْ أَجْزَأَكَ' indicates flexibility in the specific form of sacrifice, prioritizing the intent and completion of the ritual over rigid formalism.
